# Live-Friction Audit — Champion Strategy (`orb_atr` T=3.0R RB=8 ATR=0.25)

**Generated by:** `tools/audit_champion_live.py`
**Data:** 11 pairs M5, 2022-09-11 → 2026-09-11 (full 4-year set)
**Question:** Does the challenge-winning configuration contain logic bugs, and how
much of the backtest result survives real (live) trading conditions?

---

## 1. Verdict in one paragraph

The champion backtest has **no crash-level bugs** — the phase logic, daily-loss
governor, lot sizing and DST session windows all check out and reproduce exactly.
It has, however, **three optimistic modeling assumptions** that will not hold live:
(1) every signal is filled at the orb level with no re-touch check, (2) zero
spread, and (3) same-bar target/stop collisions are awarded to the *win*.
Stacked realistically, live P&L should be expected at roughly **40–55% of the
backtest**: ~$150–200/month on a raw-spread account (vs. $359/month backtested),
profit factor ~1.8–2.1 (vs. 3.55), Phase 1 in ~6–10 weeks (vs. 12 days). The edge
appears to survive friction on the three core pairs only (EURJPY, GBPJPY, XAUUSD).

---

## 2. Confirmed logic issues in the champion code path

### B1. Same-bar target/stop ambiguity resolved optimistically (real bug)
`simulate()` checks `bar.high >= target` **before** `bar.low <= stop` for longs
(and mirrored for shorts). When one M5 bar spans both levels the trade is booked
as a win. Measured: **84 of 1,812 trades (4.6%)** are ambiguous; resolving them
pessimistically (stop first) cuts P&L from $17,854 → $15,186 (−15%) and PF
3.55 → 2.94. True intrabar path is unknowable from M5 data; live truth is between
the two bounds, closer to the pessimistic bound on fast bars.

### B2. Limit fills assumed with no re-touch test (real bug, biggest impact)
A signal is "close beyond orb level"; the backtest fills **at the level** and
starts exit scanning from the next bar — without ever checking that price
returned to that level. Live limit orders left at the level go unfilled when the
breakout never pulls back. Measured: **369 of 3,220 signals (11.5%) never
re-touch the entry level**; those signals carry **$8,609 = 26.7% of total
backtest P&L, and 364/369 of them are winners** — pure adverse selection (the
best breakouts run without filling you). Alternative live style — chasing with a
market order at bar close — was simulated and **destroys the strategy**
(WR 60.2% → 17.5%, net negative): the edge *is* the limit entry at the range
boundary. Live must use limit orders and accept the missed runners.

### B3. One-position-at-a-time not modeled (capacity mismatch)
The5ers permits **one** working order / open position account-wide. The backtest
books up to 2 same-day trades whose holds **overlap in time on 249 of 1,045
trading days (~24%)** (max simultaneous = 2). Live cannot hold both; one must be
skipped or taken after the first closes. Small further haircut, and the
alphabetical priority (GBPJPY before EURJPY before XAUUSD) is arbitrary.

### B4. Pip-value constants frozen at 2024–26 mids (minor risk-drift bug)
`SPECS` hardcodes pv (GBPJPY $5.18 @193, EURJPY $6.13 @163, USDJPY $6.76 @148).
Measured yearly true pv: GBPJPY 2022 = $6.06 (**+17% undersized lots / risk in
2022**), +10% in 2023, −10% in 2026; EURJPY similar. Dollar risk per trade was
~$11–12 instead of $10 in 2022–23. Does not invalidate R-statistics but distorts
dollar P&L and phase timing slightly. Fix: compute pv per day from the pair's own
close (data already loaded).

### B5. No news blackout modeled (compliance + slippage gap)
The challenge forbids entries within 30 min of relevant red news; the backtest
trades through NFP/CPI/FOMC windows. Some backtest winners are trades a live
compliant EA cannot take, and stop exits through spikes slip more than the
0.1-pip assumption in the worst-case variant.

### B6. Minor / cosmetic
- `preprocess()` M15-ATR groups every 3 consecutive M5 bars across session gaps
  and holidays — slight ATR noise on days after gaps.
- Monthly estimate `total × 21/trading_days` counts zero-trade weekdays
  (1045 days ≈ 21.8/mo actually) — mildly understates monthly rate.
- Equity/DD sampled on closed-balance day-end only.
- `_validate_4yr.py` prints a confusing "#5" label block (cosmetic).
- `sig_vola` / `orb_half` are not the champion path; not deep-audited.

**Checked and correct:** DST helpers (EU last-Sunday March/Oct, US second-Sunday
March / first-Sunday November), London/NY wall-time windows, London-date
attribution, loader epoch handling, ATR window, orb geometry filters (2-pip min
range, 2-pip min stop, ≤3.0×ATR cap), lot rounding to 0.01 floor, fixed-$2,500
non-compounding sizing, $10 intended risk (avg loss −$9.75 confirms), max 2
trades/day account-wide, 1 trade/symbol/day, daily 5% floor with 0.5% safety
buffer, overall $2,250 floor halt, qualifying-day ≥ $12.50 and Phase-1 ≥ $2,750
with ≥3 qualifying days, forced session-end flat, deterministic ordering.

## 3. Quantified live-vs-backtest gap (champion, RB=8)

(RB=6 variant shows the same shape: baseline $331/mo → raw F2 $191/mo → G $149/mo.)

**Stacked honest estimate for live (raw account, limit entries, compliant news
filter):**
- F2 baseline − missed-limit-fill losses (~15–22% net of substitute fills)
  − ambiguity haircut (10–15%) − overlap/news skips (5–10%)
- ≈ **$135–180/month, PF ≈ 1.6–2.0, Phase 1 in ~35–55 trading days.**
- Pessimistic path (H + missed fills) ≈ **$95–130/month** — Phase 1 in ~2–3
  months. Still no time limit on The5ers, so still passable, but thin.

**Per-pair under F2 (raw):** EURJPY $3,767 · GBPJPY $3,465 · XAUUSD $3,311 ·
all other 8 pairs combined <$350. Trade the three core pairs only; drop the rest
(noise + extra exposure).

## 4. Recommended code fixes (before demo)

1. `simulate()`: require price to re-touch the entry level after the signal bar;
   unfilled signals → no trade. Add a `stop_first=True` reporting mode (or
   coin-flip) for ambiguous bars. This realigns the backtest with live limits.
2. `SPECS`: derive pv per day (`100000*0.01/close` for JPY pairs) instead of
   frozen mids.
3. Add a red-news blackout list to the backtest (CSV already defined for the EA).
4. Enforce one-open-position semantics in `run_backtest` (skip overlapping
   candidates instead of booking both).
5. Validate data provenance: the 4-year files have `volume=0` (the 2-year FSB
   files have real volume) — spot-check overlapping 2024–26 OHLC between both
   sources before trusting 2022–23 rows.

---

## 5. What this means for the challenge

The5ers $2,500 High Stakes needs +$250 (P1) and +$125 (P2) with **no time limit**
— even the pessimistic live estimate clears it. The real risks are (a) execution
quality of limit fills on a fast breakout, (b) news-window compliance, and (c)
the tiny stops (3–4 pips) making results spread-provider-sensitive. Run the
2-week MT5 demo with limit entries on **EURJPY + GBPJPY + XAUUSD only**, raw
account if available, and gate the go-live on demo ≥ ~$140/month run-rate.
